title: Trial of Family and the Rules of Divorce

paragraphs.text: There is no deity except Allah, so the believers should rely on Him. Some of their spouses and children may act as enemies to them, so they must be careful; yet if they pardon, overlook and forgive, Allah too is Forgiving and Merciful. Wealth and children are only a test, while Allah holds a great reward. Believers should fear Allah as much as they can, listen, obey and spend, for this is better for them, and whoever is saved from his own greed is truly successful. If they lend Allah a good loan, He will multiply it and forgive them, because He is Most Appreciative and Patient.

The next surah gives guidance about divorce. Men should divorce at the start of the waiting period, count it carefully and fear Allah. Women should not be driven out of their homes during this time, nor should they leave, unless they commit clear immorality. These are Allah's limits, and whoever crosses them wrongs himself, for perhaps Allah will bring about a new situation afterward. When the term is nearly over, the husband should either keep his wife kindly or part from her kindly, and two just witnesses should be present. Whoever fears Allah, He will make a way out for him and provide for him from where he never expected. Allah is enough for anyone who trusts Him.

For women who no longer menstruate, or who have not yet menstruated, the waiting period is three months, and for pregnant women it lasts until they give birth. Allah makes matters easy for whoever fears Him and increases his reward. Divorced women must be housed according to the husband's means and must not be harmed. If they nurse the child, they should be paid fairly. Each person spends according to what Allah has given, and Allah will bring ease after hardship.

Many towns rebelled against the command of their Lord and His messengers, so Allah held them to a strict account, and their final outcome was loss. People of understanding should therefore fear Him. He has sent down a reminder and a Messenger who recites clear verses, in order to bring the believers out of darkness into light and admit them into gardens forever.
